claim: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection causes significant human disease that, with no approved treatment or vaccine, constitutes a major public health concern.
source: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection causes significant human disease that, with no approved treatment or vaccine, constitutes a major public health concern.
evidence: This is a statement about the public health significance of ZIKV and the lack of approved treatments, which is established knowledge in the field.

claim: ZIKV life cycle entirely relies on the cytoplasmic fate of the viral RNA genome (vRNA) through a fine-tuned equilibrium between vRNA translation, replication, and packaging into new virions, all within virus-induced replication organelles (vROs).
source: Its life cycle entirely relies on the cytoplasmic fate of the viral RNA genome (vRNA) through a fine-tuned equilibrium between vRNA translation, replication, and packaging into new virions, all within virus-induced replication organelles (vROs).
evidence: This statement describes the general understanding of ZIKV replication based on established knowledge in virology.

claim: IGF2BP2 was identified as a new host dependency factor that regulates vRNA synthesis through an RNA interference (RNAi) mini-screening and subsequent functional characterization.
source: In this study, with an RNA interference (RNAi) mini-screening and subsequent functional characterization, we have identified insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 2 (IGF2BP2) as a new host dependency factor that regulates vRNA synthesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data from the RNAi screening and functional assays described in the manuscript.

claim: In infected cells, IGF2BP2 associates with viral NS5 polymerase and redistributes to the perinuclear viral replication compartment.
source: In infected cells, IGF2BP2 associates with viral NS5 polymerase and redistributes to the perinuclear viral replication compartment.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and confocal microscopy data presented in the manuscript.

claim: IGF2BP2 directly interacts with ZIKV vRNA 3' nontranslated region as shown by combined fluorescence in situ hybridization-based confocal imaging, in vitro binding assays, and immunoprecipitation coupled to RT-qPCR.
source: Combined fluorescence in situ hybridization-based confocal imaging, in vitro binding assays, and immunoprecipitation coupled to RT-qPCR showed that IGF2BP2 directly interacts with ZIKV vRNA 3' nontranslated region.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple experimental approaches including FISH, MST binding assays, and IP-RT-qPCR.

claim: IGF2BP2 knockdown impairs de novo vRO biogenesis as demonstrated using ZIKV sub-genomic replicons and a replication-independent vRO induction system.
source: Using ZIKV sub-genomic replicons and a replication-independent vRO induction system, we demonstrated that IGF2BP2 knockdown impairs de novo vRO biogenesis and, consistently, vRNA synthesis.
evidence: This is supported by data from replicon assays and the pIRO-Z system combined with electron microscopy.

claim: ZIKV infection alters the protein and RNA interactomes of IGF2BP2 as revealed by analysis of immunopurified IGF2BP2 complex using quantitative mass spectrometry and RT-qPCR.
source: Finally, the analysis of immunopurified IGF2BP2 complex using quantitative mass spectrometry and RT-qPCR revealed that ZIKV infection alters the protein and RNA interactomes of IGF2BP2.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data and RT-qPCR analysis of co-immunoprecipitated RNAs.

claim: ZIKV hijacks and remodels the IGF2BP2 ribonucleoprotein complex to regulate vRO biogenesis and vRNA neosynthesis.
source: Altogether, our data support that ZIKV hijacks and remodels the IGF2BP2 ribonucleoprotein complex to regulate vRO biogenesis and vRNA neosynthesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the collective experimental data presented in the study.

claim: ZIKV belongs to the Orthoflavivirus genus within the Flaviviridae family which comprises over 70 arthropod-borne viruses (arboviruses) such as dengue virus (DENV), West Nile virus (WNV), and yellow fever virus.
source: ZIKV belongs to the Orthoflavivirus genus within the Flaviviridae family which comprises over 70 arthropod-borne viruses (arboviruses) such as dengue virus (DENV), West Nile virus (WNV), and yellow fever virus.
evidence: This is established taxonomic knowledge about ZIKV classification.

claim: ZIKV is primarily transmitted to humans by Aedes spp. mosquito bites.
source: Similar to the closely related DENV, ZIKV is primarily transmitted to humans by Aedes spp. mosquito bites (Gould and Solomon, 2008)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: ZIKV can cause Guillain-Barré syndrome in adults.
source: Similar to the closely related DENV, ZIKV is primarily transmitted to humans by Aedes spp. mosquito bites (Gould and Solomon, 2008) and can cause Guillain-Barré syndrome in adults.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ZIKV pathology supported by the citation.

claim: When vertically transmitted to a fetus during pregnancy, ZIKV can infect the placenta as well as neural progenitor cells, microglial cells, and astrocytes in the developing brain.
source: When vertically transmitted to a fetus during pregnancy, this neurotropic virus can infect the placenta as well as neural progenitor cells, microglial cells, and astrocytes in the developing brain, which may eventually cause severe microcephaly in newborns (Cugola et al., 2016; Krauer et al., 2017; Nowakowski et al., 2016; Pierson and Graham, 2016; Retallack et al., 2016; Vota et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Vertical transmission of ZIKV during pregnancy may eventually cause severe microcephaly in newborns.
source: When vertically transmitted to a fetus during pregnancy, this neurotropic virus can infect the placenta as well as neural progenitor cells, microglial cells, and astrocytes in the developing brain, which may eventually cause severe microcephaly in newborns (Cugola et al., 2016; Krauer et al., 2017; Nowakowski et al., 2016; Pierson and Graham, 2016; Retallack et al., 2016; Vota et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations and is established knowledge about ZIKV pathology.

claim: No antiviral treatments against ZIKV or prophylactic vaccines are currently approved.
source: Unfortunately, no antiviral treatments against ZIKV or prophylactic vaccines are currently approved.
evidence: This is a statement of current knowledge about the state of ZIKV therapeutics.

claim: ZIKV is a single-stranded positive sense enveloped RNA virus.
source: ZIKV is a single-stranded positive sense enveloped RNA virus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ZIKV structure.

claim: The ZIKV vRNA genome is ~11-kb-long and is composed of an open reading frame flanked by 5' and 3' nontranslated regions (NTRs).
source: Its ~11-kb-long viral RNA (vRNA) genome is composed of an open reading frame flanked by 5' and 3' nontranslated regions (NTRs).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ZIKV genome structure.

claim: The vRNA plays a central role in different steps of the viral replication cycle including being translated to produce all viral proteins, used as template for genome neosynthesis, and selectively packaged into assembling viral particles.
source: The vRNA plays a central role in different steps of the viral replication cycle including being translated to produce all viral proteins, used as template for genome neosynthesis, and selectively packaged into assembling viral particles.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the role of vRNA in the viral life cycle.

claim: The vRNA, translated at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane, encodes one polyprotein which is matured into 10 viral proteins.
source: The vRNA, translated at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane, encodes one polyprotein which is matured into 10 viral proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ZIKV protein expression.

claim: Three structural proteins (C, prM, and E) together with vRNA assemble new viral particles.
source: Three structural proteins (C, prM, and E) together with vRNA assemble new viral particles
evidence: This is established knowledge about ZIKV virion assembly.

claim: Seven nonstructural proteins (NS1, NS2A, NS2B, NS3, NS4A, NS4B, and NS5) are responsible for vRNA neosynthesis, via the activity of the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) NS5 along with the contribution of other viral proteins and host factors.
source: and seven nonstructural proteins (NS1, NS2A, NS2B, NS3, NS4A, NS4B, and NS5) are responsible for vRNA neosynthesis, via the activity of the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) NS5 along with the contribution of other viral proteins and host factors (Acosta et al., 2014; Mazeaud et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research and is established knowledge.

claim: Orthoflaviviruses have evolved to establish a fine-tuned equilibrium between vRNA translation, replication, and encapsidation steps since they cannot occur simultaneously.
source: To efficiently replicate, orthoflaviviruses have evolved to establish a fine-tuned equilibrium between vRNA translation, replication, and encapsidation steps since they cannot occur simultaneously.
evidence: This is established knowledge about orthoflavivirus replication strategy.

claim: The mechanisms underlying the spatiotemporal fate of vRNA remain elusive.
source: However, the mechanisms underlying the spatiotemporal fate of vRNA remain elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Viral replication processes occur in viral replication organelles (vRO) which result from major alterations of the ER.
source: These processes occur in viral replication organelles (vRO) which result from major alterations of the ER
evidence: This is established knowledge about orthoflavivirus replication.

claim: vROs are believed to coordinate in time and space the steps of the life cycle, notably through the spatial segregation of the vRNA, at different steps of the life cycle.
source: and are believed to coordinate in time and space the steps of the life cycle, notably through the spatial segregation of the vRNA, at different steps of the life cycle.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on current understanding in the field.

claim: vROs accumulate in a large cage-like compartment which is located in the perinuclear area.
source: vROs accumulate in a large cage-like compartment which is located in the perinuclear area (Cortese et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Three architectures of viral organelles-like ultrastructures have been described: vesicle packets (VP), virus bags (VB), and convoluted membranes (CM).
source: Three architectures of these viral organelles-like ultrastructures have been described: vesicle packets (VP), virus bags (VB), and convoluted membranes (CM).
evidence: This is established knowledge about vRO morphology.

claim: The VPs resulting from ER invagination are spherical vesicles with a diameter of approximately 90 nm connected to the cytosol through a 10-nm-wide pore-like opening.
source: The VPs resulting from ER invagination are spherical vesicles with a diameter of approximately 90 nm connected to the cytosol through a 10-nm-wide pore-like opening (Cortese et al., 2017; Hamel et al., 2015; Paul and Bartenschlager, 2013; Welsch et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: VPs are believed to host vRNA synthesis.
source: They are believed to host vRNA synthesis.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on current understanding in the field.

claim: The nonstructural proteins NS5, NS3, NS1, NS4A, and NS4B, absolutely required for vRNA replication, and also double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), the vRNA replication intermediate, are enriched in VPs as imaged by immunogold labeling followed by transmission electron microscopy.
source: Indeed, the nonstructural proteins NS5, NS3, NS1, NS4A, and NS4B, absolutely required for vRNA replication, and also double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), the vRNA replication intermediate, are enriched in VPs as imaged by immunogold labeling followed by transmission electron microscopy (Chatel-Chaix et al., 2016; Welsch et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: It has been proposed that the RNA genome exit VPs through their pore to be directly packaged into assembling particles budding into the ER lumen.
source: It has been proposed that the RNA genome exit VPs through their pore to be directly packaged into assembling particles budding into the ER lumen.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on current understanding in the field.

claim: Immature virions geometrically accumulate in dilated ER cisternae referred to as VBs.
source: Immature virions geometrically accumulate in dilated ER cisternae referred to as VBs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ZIKV assembly.

claim: The viral and cellular determinants of vRO biogenesis are poorly understood mostly because this process will be impacted (even indirectly) by any perturbations of viral replication efficiency and hence, viral factors abundance.
source: The viral and cellular determinants of vRO biogenesis are poorly understood mostly because this process will be impacted (even indirectly) by any perturbations of viral replication efficiency and hence, viral factors abundance.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge and challenges in the field.

claim: The recent advent of replication-independent VP induction systems identified several determinants of de novo VP biogenesis, most notably including ZIKV NS4A, NS1, and 3' NTR RNA, as well as host factors ATL2, VCP, and RACK1.
source: The recent advent of replication-independent VP induction systems identified several determinants of de novo VP biogenesis, most notably including ZIKV NS4A, NS1, and 3' NTR RNA, as well as host factors ATL2, VCP, and RACK1 (Cerikan et al., 2020; Cortese et al., 2021; Goellner et al., 2020; Mazeaud et al., 2021; Neufeldt et al., 2019; Płaszczyca et al., 2019; Shue et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to recent research.

claim: Multiple reports have shown that cellular RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate the replication, translation, and/or encapsidation of vRNA often through associations with 5' or 3' NTRs.
source: Multiple reports have shown that cellular RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate the replication, translation, and/or encapsidation of vRNA often through associations with 5' or 3' NTRs (for review, see Mazeaud et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: YBX1 associates with 3' NTR of DENV vRNA and regulates both vRNA translation and viral particle production.
source: For instance, YBX1 associates with 3' NTR of DENV vRNA and regulates both vRNA translation and viral particle production (Diosa-Toro et al., 2022; Paranjape and Harris, 2007; Phillips et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: In case of the hepatitis C virus (HCV), it was shown that the YBX1 RNP comprising HCV vRNA, IGF2BP2, LARP1, DDX6, and other cell proteins regulates the equilibrium between vRNA replication and infectious particle production.
source: In case of the hepatitis C virus (HCV), a Flaviviridae from the Hepacivirus genus, it was shown that the YBX1 RNP comprising HCV vRNA, IGF2BP2, LARP1, DDX6, and other cell proteins regulates the equilibrium between vRNA replication and infectious particle production (Chatel-Chaix et al., 2013; Chatel-Chaix et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: It is unknown whether the co-opting mechanism of RNP complexes is conserved in the Orthoflavivirus genus.
source: However, it is unknown whether this is a conserved co-opting mechanism in the Orthoflavivirus genus (which also belongs to the Flaviviridae family)
evidence: This is a statement about a gap in current knowledge.

claim: It is unknown whether orthoflaviviruses modulate the composition of RNP complexes to rewire their functions in favor of replication.
source: and if so, whether these viruses modulate the composition of this complex to rewire its functions in favor of replication.
evidence: This is a statement about a gap in current knowledge.

claim: The 3' NTR of vRNA is a key player of vRO morphogenesis.
source: Finally, considering that the 3' NTR of vRNA is a key player of vRO morphogenesis (Cerikan et al., 2020)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: vRO biogenesis involves host vRNA-binding proteins prior to vRNA synthesis.
source: this raises the hypothesis that this viral process involves host vRNA-binding proteins prior to vRNA synthesis.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on existing knowledge.

claim: None of the tested shRNAs had any impact on cell viability as measured by MTT assays.
source: None of these shRNA had any impact on cell viability as measured by 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) assays (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The KD of DEAD-box helicases RHA, DDX6, DDX21, or DDX5 had no significant impact in virus production when compared to the non-target control shRNA.
source: The KD of DEAD-box helicases RHA (RNA helicase A, also named DHX9), DDX6, DDX21, or DDX5 had no significant impact in virus production when compared to the non-target control shRNA (shNT).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from plaque assays shown in Figure 1B-D.

claim: The KD of IGF2BP2 resulted in significant decrease in the titers of both ZIKV strains.
source: In contrast, the KD of IGF2BP2 and LARP1 resulted in significant decrease and increase in the titers of both ZIKV strains, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from plaque assays shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: The KD of LARP1 resulted in significant increase in the titers of both ZIKV strains.
source: In contrast, the KD of IGF2BP2 and LARP1 resulted in significant decrease and increase in the titers of both ZIKV strains, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from plaque assays shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: The observed phenotypes of IGF2BP2 and LARP1 KD were specific to ZIKV since no significant impact was observed for DENV.
source: The observed phenotypes were specific to ZIKV since no significant impact was observed for DENV (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from plaque assays shown in Figure 1B-D.

claim: IGF2BP2 KD resulted in a significant 60% decrease in ZIKV-R2A viral replication.
source: IGF2BP2 KD resulted in a significant 60% decrease in viral replication.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from luciferase assays shown in Figure 1F.

claim: LARP1 KD had no stimulatory effect on ZIKV-R2A viral replication, suggesting a role of this host factor in virus assembly and/or release.
source: In contrast, LARP1 KD had no stimulatory effect on viral replication, suggesting a role of this host factor in virus assembly and/or release.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data from luciferase assays.

claim: YBX1, YBX2, and DDX3 KD all resulted in a decrease in ZIKV replication although this did not translate into impacts in virus titers.
source: Of note YBX1, YBX2, and DDX3 KD all resulted in a decrease in ZIKV replication although this did not translate into impacts in virus titers (Figure 1B–F).

claim: IGF2BP2 was efficiently knocked down upon transduction at both protein and mRNA levels.
source: First, western blotting and RT-qPCR with transduced Huh7.5 cell lysates validated that IGF2BP2 was efficiently knocked down upon transduction at both protein and mRNA levels (Figure 2A and B)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: IGF2BP2 KD correlated with a 74% decrease in ZIKV production.
source: which correlated with a 74% decrease in ZIKV production (Figure 2C)

claim: IGF2BP2 KD resulted in reductions in the expression of viral proteins NS3, NS4A, and NS5.
source: which correlated with a 74% decrease in ZIKV production (Figure 2C) and reductions in the expression of viral proteins NS3, NS4A, and NS5 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Comparable impairment of ZIKV titers upon IGF2BP2 KD was observed in human immortalized astrocytes (NHA-hTERT).
source: Comparable impairment of ZIKV titers upon IGF2BP2 KD was observed in other cell lines relevant for ZIKV pathogenesis, namely human immortalized astrocytes (NHA-hTERT; Figure 2D)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Comparable impairment of ZIKV titers upon IGF2BP2 KD was observed in cancer-derived trophoblasts (JEG-3).
source: Comparable impairment of ZIKV titers upon IGF2BP2 KD was observed in other cell lines relevant for ZIKV pathogenesis, namely human immortalized astrocytes (NHA-hTERT; Figure 2D) and cancer-derived trophoblasts (JEG-3; Figure 2E)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Comparable impairment of ZIKV titers upon IGF2BP2 KD was observed for ZIKV FSS13025 strain in Huh7.5 cells.

claim: IGF2BP2 KD did not change the production of DENV1, DENV2, or DENV4.

claim: DENV3 replication was only slightly decreased upon IGF2BP2 KD.
source: IGF2BP2 KD did not change the production of DENV1, DENV2, or DENV4, while DENV3 replication was only slightly decreased (Figure 3B–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B-E.

claim: IGF2BP2 KD had no impact on the replication of WNV.
source: Finally, IGF2BP2 KD had no impact on the replication of either WNV, another orthoflavivirus (Figure 3F)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: IGF2BP2 KD had no impact on the replication of SARS-CoV-2.
source: or of SARS-CoV-2, another positive-strand RNA virus from the Coronaviridae family (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: IGF2BP2 is a specific host dependency factor for ZIKV replication.
source: Overall, these data clearly show that the IGF2BP2 is a specific host dependency factor for ZIKV replication.
evidence: This is an inference based on the collective experimental data showing specificity for ZIKV.

source: correlating with a partial colocalization with NS3 and dsRNA (Manders' coefficients of 0.45±0.04 and 0.46±0.04, respectively).

source: IGF2BP2 along with IGF2BP1 and IGF2BP3 paralogues are highly conserved oncofetal RBPs belonging to the insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein family
